neighbours.label: the token right after a short quoted reply or reveal in narrative dialogue (the ', and' / ',' / ':' that resumes narration)
fire: "Where are you going?" the old man asked. "Home," the boy said, and he ran down the hill.
"Do you regret it?" she asked quietly. "No," he murmured, "not for a single day."
"What is your name?" the guard demanded. "Thomas," he answered, and the gate swung open.
"Who sent you?" the queen asked. "The king," the messenger replied, and bowed low.
"Are you afraid?" her father asked. "Yes," she whispered, "but I will go anyway."
"What did the doctor say?" Ma asked. "Rest," Pa said, and he sat down by the fire.
"Which way to the river?" the traveler asked. "East," the farmer said, and pointed.
"Is it over?" the soldier asked. "Almost," the captain replied, and lit a cigarette.
quiet: The old man asked where the boy was going, and the boy said he was going home before he ran down the hill.
She asked him quietly whether he regretted it, and he told her he had never regretted it.
The guard demanded to know his name, and when Thomas told him, the gate swung open.
The queen asked who had sent the messenger, and he explained that the king had sent him.
Her father asked whether she was afraid, and she admitted she was but said she would go.
Ma asked what the doctor had said, and Pa told her he needed rest before sitting by the fire.
The traveler asked the farmer the way to the river, and the farmer pointed toward the east.
The soldier asked whether it was over, and the captain told him it almost was.

notes: Top examples: ' and' / ',' / ':' right after a one-word quoted answer or a reveal ('The name of that student: Albert Einstein'). Probes ~0.41-0.44 on quoted replies, 0.07-0.12 on reported speech.
